title: Kinesis and dependent AWS services disruption in US-EAST-1
investigation_summary: Kinesis and services relying on its event or metric paths experienced errors, delays, and backlogs; AWS documented Lambda invocation errors and host memory contention.
symptoms: CloudWatch Events/EventBridge API errors and delivery delays
technical_root_cause: Adding capacity to the Kinesis front-end fleet caused existing servers to establish per-server communication threads with new servers. Fleet growth pushed thread counts above the operating-system limit; shard-map cache construction then failed, leaving front-end servers unable to route requests to backend clusters. AWS explicitly ruled out the initially suspected memory-pressure explanation as the Kinesis root cause.
customer_impact: Kinesis errors affected dependent services. Cognito users experienced elevated API failures and could be unable to authenticate or obtain temporary credentials; CloudWatch metric/log APIs had errors and latency with gaps in persisted telemetry; Lambda invocation errors increased from local metric-buffer memory contention; EventBridge, ECS/EKS provisioning and scaling workflows were delayed.
business_impact: AWS customers experienced impaired streaming, authentication/credential, monitoring, serverless invocation, and container orchestration workflows. AWS did not publish a customer count or revenue loss.
recovery_actions: Removed the capacity addition, then restarted Kinesis front-end servers gradually to rebuild shard-map caches and restore traffic; Kinesis returned to normal at 10:23 PM PST.
Deployed a Cognito change to reduce dependency on Kinesis; Cognito returned to normal by 2:18 PM PST.
Mitigated Lambda invocation errors caused by local metric-buffer memory contention at 10:36 AM PST.
preventive_actions: Move to larger CPU/memory servers and reduce fleet thread demand.
Add fine-grained thread-consumption alarms and test a higher OS thread limit.
Improve cold starts and move shard-map cache to a dedicated fleet.
Partition front-end fleets for large dependent AWS services and accelerate cellularization.
Change Cognito so Kinesis errors do not exhaust its buffers.
Persist three hours of metric data locally in CloudWatch; change completed in us-east-1 at publication time.

sources.evidence_notes: AWS post-event summary states capacity addition, OS thread limit exhaustion, failed shard-map construction, dependent Cognito/CloudWatch/Lambda/EventBridge impacts, recovery timelines, and preventive measures; AWS specifically says Kinesis root cause was not memory pressure.

title: Google Cloud australia-southeast2 multi-service incident
investigation_summary: Multiple Google Cloud products degraded in australia-southeast2. Apigee errors and latency rose, Batch jobs remained scheduled, and connectivity-sensitive operations failed.
technical_root_cause: Two nearby fiber failures reduced available inter-region capacity; then a voltage swell at a network PoP hosting 50% of regional network capacity rebooted networking devices. Equipment rectifiers shut down because a UPS voltage regulator pushed voltage above the equipment tolerance.
customer_impact: Incident 16:21–19:34 PDT; longest regional impact 2h03.
business_impact: Incident 16:21–19:34 PDT; longest regional impact 2h03.
recovery_actions: Impacted network paths recovered after devices rebooted; all affected zones regained full connectivity by 16:43 US/Pacific. Some services required manual recovery actions.
preventive_actions: Review regional power distribution and add protections against voltage swells/sags.
Reconfigure UPS voltage regulator and institute monthly reviews.
Deploy double-conversion UPS.
Change network-device configuration to reduce recovery time.
Review other sites for the same risk.

sources.evidence_notes: Final Google report updated 4 Dec 2024 documents two fiber failures, voltage swell, 50% capacity PoP, device reboot, 21-minute multi-product loss, up to 15% latency/error-rate increase, root cause, and prevention.
